builderChecks: Exactly three light roles exist outdoors: Moonlight_Main (cold key), the facade's warm house glow (02 section, untouched here), LightningFlashLight (cold, 0 at rest). Any fourth light in the yard fails this section.
No entry in this manifest uses a warm colour except where it REFERENCES the facade's own glow entries. AmbientNight_Fill must stay in the #0B1D2A-#14313F range.
Object names LightningSkyFlash, LightningFlashLight, LightningController are exact — Lightning.lua finds them by GameObject.Find.
MoonDisc sits north of the facade (Z > 30) and above the roofline from spawn's view; it is emissive backdrop only and is NOT the scene light.
Lightning rest state: LightningSkyFlash invisible, LightningFlashLight intensity 0.
coordinateSystem: Same as 01-layout: 1 unit = 1 floor tile, X east, Z north, Y up, floor top Y=0, plot 40 (X) x 30 (Z), house facade zone at Z 23-30. Sky entries are scene-level: positions are anchors/directions, not floor placements.

settings.build: Scene skybox/backdrop: a large inverted dome (or the Studio scene skybox slot) painted as a night storm sky — near-black blue at the zenith (#060D16) grading to deep blue-teal at the horizon (#14313F). Heavy cloud cover baked into the dome texture; no stars visible through the storm except around the moon break.
settings.notes: Radius is far beyond the 40x30 plot so the dome never clips the facade (facade tops out under Y ~12) or the cloud layers. If Studio's skybox slot is used instead of a dome mesh, use the same colours/gradient and delete the mesh — one or the other, never both.

settings.build: Wide, flat, dark cloud-mass planes/billboards (primitives + transparent storm-cloud texture, or clustered flattened dark ellipsoids) drifting VERY slowly east. Colour #101E29 with moonlit top edges #5E707A on the north side (facing the moon).
settings.coverage: Full sky over the plot, densest over the house (north). Breaks only around MoonDisc.
settings.notes: Slow enough to read as a storm hanging overhead, not weather flying past. Keep above Y 30 so it never intersects the facade or trees.

settings.build: Second, higher, thinner cloud layer (#1C2F3D), drifting slightly faster than the low layer for parallax. This is the layer that veils and un-veils the moon.
settings.notes: Parallax between the two layers is what sells 'storm' instead of a flat painted sky.

settings.build: One pale full-moon disc (#DCE9F5, soft emissive) placed NORTH, high, BEHIND the house roofline — the poster composition (REFERENCE S2: full moon behind the roof). From the spawn point (20,0,3) looking north it sits just over the roof ridge, partly veiled by StormCloudLayer_High.
settings.emissive: Low steady glow — it is a backdrop disc, NOT a light source. The actual light is Moonlight_Main.
settings.notes: Do not add a second moon, stars around it, or a halo ring; the film sky reads as cloud + one moon.

settings.direction: From behind and above the house (north-high, same direction as the poster's rim light and the facade's MoonRimLight) shining south and down across the yard toward spawn: direction vector approx (0, -1.6, -1.1) (from position anchor (20, 30, 44) toward (20, 0, 4)).
settings.intensity: Moderate — bright enough to play by, dark enough to stay night. Tune in Play so faces/tables read clearly but shadows stay deep blue, never grey daylight.
settings.notes: Implemented as the scene's directional light / Studio lighting setting (see ATMOSPHERE.md 'How this is built in Studio'). There is exactly ONE key light outdoors. No warm fill, no per-zone accent lights in the yard.
settings.role: THE main light of the world outdoors. Cold moonlight falling on the players, the yard, the walkway and the game dressing.
settings.shadows: On if the scene budget allows — long shadows of the trees and players stretching south toward the street is the film look. If shadows cost too much performance, keep them on the trees/house only.

settings.intensity: Very low — a floor, not a light source. If a surface's colour is doing the work, this is set too high.
settings.notes: This entry is the formal replacement for DESIGN S1's 'warm ambient overall' in the yard. It must never be warmed up to compensate for a dark scene — raise Moonlight_Main instead.
settings.role: Bare-minimum cold fill so unlit corners read as deep blue night instead of pure black voids.

settings.build: Low, thin, pale blue-grey mist: a few large soft transparent planes (or scene fog + mist billboards) hugging the ground at the base of the house and drifting a little across the walkway. REFERENCE: 'Ground mist/dust: pale blue-grey, low at the base.'
settings.color: Pale blue-grey (#8FA6B5 at very low opacity)
settings.height_band_units: Y 0 to ~1.2, densest at the facade base (Z 23-28), thinning toward spawn
settings.notes: Mist is COLD like everything else outdoors. It must stay thin enough that the walkway, signs (KEEP AWAY / BEWARE) and table rings stay readable.

settings.build: The visible flash surface the Lightning.lua script drives: a very large, soft, transparent white-blue panel (or a reserved emissive patch of the sky dome) behind/above the house, starting at opacity/emissive 0 (invisible). During a strike the script pulses it so the storm clouds light up from behind, silhouetting the roof and trees.
settings.driven_by: Lightning.lua (object name must stay exactly 'LightningSkyFlash' — the script finds it by name).
settings.rest_state: Fully transparent / emissive 0. If it is visible at rest, it is wrong.

settings.build: One cold white-blue light source, intensity 0 at rest, positioned high behind the house so a flash throws the house/trees into silhouette and briefly lifts the whole yard. The script pulses it together with LightningSkyFlash.
settings.notes: Yard/sky side only. No matching flash light inside the house interior.
settings.peak_intensity: High but brief (script curve peaks ~2.2x Moonlight_Main's feel) — a flash, not a lamp.

settings.build: Empty scene object named exactly 'LightningController'; attach Lightning.lua to it. Invisible, no collider, never rendered.

flash_cycle.duty_cycle: Under ~5% of the time lit — a storm that flashes constantly reads as a disco, not weather.
flash_cycle.pattern: double flash: strike 1 quick (rise ~0.06s, fall ~0.09s), short dark gap (~0.08s), strike 2 brighter (~55% stronger) with a ~0.45s decay tail

settings.script: 11-atmosphere/Lightning.lua (--!Type(ClientAndServer): server picks the timing and fires the verified FireAllClients event; every client renders the same flash curve locally).

palette.fog: Pale blue-grey (REFERENCE ground mist), low at the house base
palette.moonlight: #B9CFEA (cold blue-silver — THE light on the players and yard)
palette.stormClouds: #101E29 to #1C2F3D (dark blue-grey cloud masses, pale moonlit edges #5E707A)
palette.warmLight_rule: NO warm ambient, NO warm fill anywhere in the yard. The only warm light in the scene is the house glow owned by 02-house-facade: EyeWindow_Left_Flat + EyeWindow_Right_4Pane (#FFA63D), EyeHalo_Left/EyeHalo_Right, and DoorLight_Pool (#FFD76A, REST LAYER ONLY — off in the default monster state).

rules.facade_coordination: 02-house-facade has a part named MoonRimLight (pale rim accent ON the house, from behind/above the roof). That stays facade-local. This section's Moonlight_Main uses the SAME moon direction (from behind/above the house, north-high, shining south over the yard) so the rim on the house and the light on the players read as one moon.
rules.lightning_scope: Lightning lights the SKY and the YARD side only. It must not flash inside the house interior (separate enclosed space, interior crew's section).
rules.supersedes_design_s1: DESIGN.md S1 says 'Warm ambient overall; each zone gets its own accent color.' For the YARD that line is superseded (user spec 2026-11-22): yard ambient is COLD blue-teal night, zone separation outdoors comes from the moonlight + house glow contrast, not warm accents. Casino accent colours survive only as materials/signage on the game dressing, never as warm light cast on the yard. Interior lighting (games now inside the house) belongs to the interior section and is out of scope here.
three_light_sources_only: 1. MOONLIGHT (cold, #B9CFEA) — the key light on players, yard, and tables.
2. HOUSE GLOW (warm) — background only, owned by 02-house-facade; this section never adds a warm source.
3. LIGHTNING (cold white-blue) — brief scripted flashes, seconds apart at random, never constant, never warm.

sourceOfTruth: User spec 2026-11-22: storm sky backdrop, lightning flashes, moonlight as the light on the players/yard, and the ONLY warm glow comes from the house in the background.
repo/00-reference/REFERENCE.md — night palette + poster sky (deep blue-teal night, full moon behind the roof, pale-blue moon rim light, low ground mist).
DESIGN.md S1 lighting plan — SUPERSEDED for the yard by this section (see rules.supersedes_design_s1). Interior lighting is the interior crew's section, not this one.
title: Monster House world — storm sky, moonlight & lightning (scene atmosphere)
